utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-67-T, the Prosecutor versus Vojislav Seselj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Registrar. We have started a few minutes late because the previous hearing finished a few minutes late on the schedule, so we are starting only now. Following a decision from the Trial Chamber, I would like to say that the public order of redaction that had been issued on the 8th of April, 2008 [as interpreted], dealing with page 29509 of the transcript in the English version, has to become confidential in order to protect the people that were mentioned on that page. There you go. Secondly, the Prosecutor has an hour and 36 minutes left, and Mr. Seselj will have his two hours. Given that we are very short of time, I'm asking everyone to use their time to the best of their abilities. And if there are objections that are not justified, the time will be deducted. So, Ms. Biersay, please proceed with your questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Rankic.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'd like to start just by giving two little reminders. I know that we don't speak the same language, but you do understand some English. If you could just -- that's right, you do understand some English? You're nodding your head. You have to say out loud. But if you just wait for the translation before you answer, it will be helpful, even if you understand what I'm saying. Do you understand? You have to answer out loud. Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand a little, but really very little.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Okay, so it shouldn't be a big problem for us. The second thing I wanted to clarify was something you described to the Trial Chamber yesterday about your Defence statements. Do you recall how many Defence statements you provided to the associates of the accused?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember well, two or three.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now, do you recall when you gave them?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Beginning with 2007, through 2008.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: If I could ask the Registrar to call up in e-court the subpoena objection, going to the last page. I wanted to show Mr. Rankic this.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Do you recognise that signature at the bottom of that page?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Whose signature is it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now, for the record, this is -- if we could go to the first page in the B/C/S as well as English.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: That is objection to the subpoena that was issued to you December 4th of 2007, and the date on it is 24 December 2007; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now, you described to the Trial Chamber that you had prepared the previous -- all the statements you gave to the Defence, and I believe you said that your son had helped you to type them up. Did you also prepare this one?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To draft this document, I had the assistance of my legal counsel, who is my close friend. He is a lawyer. And I have absolutely no legal knowledge, so somebody had to help me with the legal clauses.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what's the name of your friend?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do I have to say it in open session?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: It is necessary, Your Honour. I'd be happy to go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's move to closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And for the Court's information, we, too, are interested in the events that happened in that time-period. What became very clear yesterday is that this witness is now departing from his previous statements about those events, and that will be the crux of my examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Mr. Rankic, you were contacted by OTP investigators in March of 2003, correct, the very first time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember well, it was in August 2003.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Okay. I'm not going to argue with you. But to the extent that our internal records show something else, let's take your date, August 2003. You were contacted by investigators, and they asked you to come to a formal interview; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, that's the date of my first statement. I believe it's dated August 2003.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Mr. Rankic, so that we don't have to -- the Prosecution asks the Court to bring you back here at another occasion to complete your testimony, it's important that you listen to my questions. To the extent that I ask you for a yes or no, just say yes or no, and I will follow up with more, if needed. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: You were contacted by OTP investigators, and they invited you to come to the office in Belgrade for a meeting, an interview; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Did you go to the OTP office in Belgrade in August of 2003?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But before that, they called my family and threatened my family, that unless I come, I will be brought in by the police. That means they'll bring me in by force.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'll be forced to ask the Court to bring you back if we can't get through this in time today, so again I will ask you to answer with yes or no. The question to you is: Were you invited to come to a meeting with members of the Office of the Prosecutor in August of 2003?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I came to the interview.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Were you escorted to the interview by police from your house?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's why I went on my own two feet, to protect my family.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: It's yes or no.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not escorted by the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And from your house, were you escorted by any OTP representative?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: When you went to the office, you met -- isn't it true you met with Investigator Paolo Pastore Stocchi and Investigator Sabine Shulz? You have to say, Yes, into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: There was also a translator there to assist with the communication between the three of you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: The representatives of the OTP, the investigators, asked you questions about what you knew about the events of 1990, 1991, and 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Something like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: They asked you about what you did during that time-period; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but also before that period, my entire life.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And they asked you a lot of questions; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And you answered them to the best of your ability; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: In the room, at any time, were you beaten by these investigators?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And I see you laughing at that. It sounds ridiculous to you, does it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is ridiculous.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Were any of the investigators armed?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I noticed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And, again, you're laughing because it sounds ridiculous to you, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is the first time I hear of the notion of armed investigators.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So you gave a lot of information to the investigators in August of 2003, and it was reduced to writing; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And when you tried to give the information, you tried to give it in a chronological order of when things happened; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I tried to follow the chronology to the best of my recollection.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And the investigators told you, Follow the -- stick to the chronology; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they asked questions haphazardly, while I tried to keep to the chronology.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Your statement, which is in your binder under tab 1, after you gave the information to the investigators, they produced a document in English; correct? And that is 65 ter 7538, and it's in the Court's binder 1 at tab 1, if the Court would like to follow the hard copy. So what you -- the information you gave to the investigators, that was reduced to a written statement; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If Madam Biersay gave me leave, I could explain this, and I'll try to be very brief.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: But what I want to know is: They produced for you a written statement; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was at the end of day 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now, according to the statement, you were interviewed on the 4th and the 5th of August, 2003. Does that refresh your recollection about how many days it was?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly, then it was at the end of day two.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So it was reduced to a written format; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: The interpreter assisted in explaining to you the contents of the written statement that was in English; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before that, the interpreter read back to me from the laptop, what I had stated, while the questioning was still underway.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And at the end, you were presented with a document from those two days of interviews, and you signed that document; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: One step at a time. You signed the document; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but you're not letting me explain.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'm asking you yes-or-no questions. You signed the document on all pages, and you signed it at the very end; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And the interpreter also signed, and she signed on page 19 in the English, 18 in the B/C/S. What she signed on the 5th of August, 2003: "Zoran Rankic has acknowledged that the facts and matters set out in his statement, as translated by me, are true to the best of his knowledge and recollection, and has accordingly signed his signature where indicated." You're turning the pages rather slowly. It is on page 18, as I said before, and I am --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Eighteen.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Number 4. You see that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now, between day 4 -- between the 4th and the 5th of August, you were allowed to go home at the end of the interview?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I was not planning to ask any questions of a technical nature, because I will recuse myself regarding the part invoking Carla Del Ponte on contempt issues. So I have to remain very general on my questions, but I have just a technical question to ask you regarding a document that was signed by the interpreter. The interpreter, and I'm not giving her name, states that she hereby has translated the facts and the topics that were touched upon in your statement, so what I would like to know: When the 19 pages were translated into English, I was wondering whether the interpreter translated into your own language the entirety of the 85 paragraphs, which could take some time. Has she done that; yes or no? Has she said, Mr. Rankic, we are going to show you a document in English, a document of exactly 17 pages; I'm going to translate the entirety of the document. First paragraph, and then she translates in your own language the first paragraph. And the second paragraph, My name is Zoran Rankic, I'm Serb. And she translated that into your own language. And the third paragraph, You were conscripted within the JNA in 1976 [as interpreted]. And fourth paragraph, and so on and so forth. Has she done that? Has she translated the whole document, one paragraph after another, and thereafter you signed the 17 pages? This is the question that I would like to put to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, while the interview was underway she was reading to me from the laptop, and later on she said that all of that would be merged and brought to me for my signature in Serbian. And I asked for all that to be shown to me, but the statement was never given to me in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So you are saying to us, and this is important, that the full 17 pages were not translated to you by the interpreter before you signed at the end of the document. But during questions and answers put by the investigators, questions were interpreted to you and all the discussions were interpreted to you, but the interpreter did not read all 17 pages in your own language. It is very important.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, we did not understand each other. She did bring me the translation of all the 17 pages, and I signed, but I asked for a copy to be submitted to me subsequently. At 7.00 in the evening, after two days of questioning, my psychological state was not the best, and I could not concentrate any more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So you're saying that she brought a translation in your own language of all 17 pages. So why is it that you did not sign this document in B/C/S if you had a B/C/S version of that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I signed what they asked me to sign.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Ms. Biersay, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Just to clarify, when you signed on August 5th of 2003, did you see a B/C/S version of the statement that you'd signed in English?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now, let's fast-forward now to January of 2004. Again in Belgrade, you received a scheduling call for another interview; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again through my family.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So are you saying that the investigators didn't speak to you directly about coming in for an interview in January of 2004; is that what you're telling the Court?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of the contacts were through my family.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And again you went to the interview; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in order to avoid any consequences that might have arisen.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Mr. Rankic, I'd appreciate it if you kept your answers to match my questions. Now, when you went to the same office to have this interview, this time there are two totally different investigators from the OTP; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And a totally different interpreter; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that there was a different interpreter, if my memory serves me well.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And this is in e-court as 65 ter 7539, and it should be in binder 1, tab 2, for the Court.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And in this statement that you gave, you specifically were shown your previous statement from 2003 and asked to make corrections and clarifications to the 2003 statement; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Turn to tab 2 of your binder, please. And if you could look at paragraph 3, paragraph 3. Mr. Rankic does seem to take a lot of time in getting to the places that I direct him to, so I wonder if the usher could stand by him, perhaps, to assist and make this a little bit more speedy. Now, in paragraph 3 of your 2004 statement, it specifically says that you were provided with a signed -- that you were provided with a copy of that signed statement and that you were asked to clarify some issues discussed in that previous statement; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's what is written here. Perhaps, but I was never provided with that copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Ms. Biersay, could you enlighten us whether the copy that the witness was given was in English or B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: The copy, as the Court will see, as the signed version, is the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So, in your 2004 statement, you clarified what you told them in August of 2003; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were some more questions and more questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Let's turn to paragraph 17 of your 2004 statement. In paragraph 23, and I'm quoting: "I would like to delete the sentence reading, 'The two republican ministries existed at the time. It was not at the federal level.' This is a mistake and doesn't make any sense to me." Do you see that? So you corrected the 2003 statement that was presented to you again in 2004; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whatever was shown to me was on the laptop.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Okay. You were shown -- whether it's an electronic version or a hard-copy version, you were shown your previous statement and you were allowed to make corrections to it; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You did not allow me to say at the very beginning how everything transpired, so it is pointless for me to go on explaining what happened next. You did not allow me an introduction into what I was going to say next.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And you signed the 2004 statement as well in English; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I signed all the statements that I provided. Let's not waste any more time on whether I signed or not. I signed all of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So this interview was conducted on the 17th, 18th, and 19th of January of 2004; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And at the end of each day, you went home, and you would come back the next day; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And at no time in 2003 did you report any allegations about the OTP threatening you. Did you do that in 2003?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. Who do you think I should have turned to and report them?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'm asking you a question. Did you go to the police with reports about OTP misconduct in 2003; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is really preposterous. This is funny.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For me to report an international organisation to the Serbian police?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Did you go to a local newspaper to let them know what was happening? Did you do that in 2003?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. My honour would not allow me to do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: You didn't report these allegations in 2003; you didn't report them in 2004; and you didn't report them in 2005. Is that right? You have to answer --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. I was waiting to come here to the Tribunal and present all that before the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Did you write the Trial Chamber to tell them about what was happening? Did you call the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was waiting for the regular procedure to continue for me to come to the court.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now, in June of 2006, on the 13th, you met again with Investigator Stocchi -- Pastore Stocchi, and you met with attorney Dan Saxon, and the purpose of that meeting was to finalise a statement that would be used for your testimony in this case; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And you began that process in June 2006, but it was not completed, the statement was not completed in June of 2006; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And that is because you told them and reported that you had been approached by a group of people in Belgrade and told not to play with your life; right? You reported threats to you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a fabrication.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And didn't you also tell them that your son had answered the phone and someone threatened to blow you up? Didn't you tell them that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did say that, but that has nothing whatsoever to do with the Serbian Radical Party. It had to do with an idiot who was a protected witness here. Let me not mention his name.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Mr. Rankic, I'm confused. Before, you said that's a total fabrication; and then you said that you did say that. Which one is it? Is it a fabrication, or did you tell the investigators that there were threats against you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What the investigator said is not correct. However, what my son told me, that is correct, because there was an idiot who threatened him on the phone.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And you also told them that you thought not that it was connected with the SRS or anyone else, that it was connected with your co-operation with the OTP? That's what you told them in 2006; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I thought at the time. Later on, I realised that it was something else.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: But that's what you told them. And out of concern for your safety, as early as June 2006, there was a discussion about relocating you for your own safety; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was just one of the reasons.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And, in fact, you even assisted them in identifying the country to which you would prefer to be relocated. You told them that you wanted to go to Sweden; right? In 2006, you told them that you wanted to be relocated to Sweden because you knew people there.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: The Victim and Witness Unit did a threat assessment with you in July of 2006, again about the issue of relocating you to Sweden; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what they did, but it all came to nothing.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: In September of 2006 -- I'm now directing your attention to the first statement that you signed in your language, and that was the 89(F) statement that's in your binder behind tab 3. We talked about it yesterday. Now, on the 18th and 19th of September, you were interviewed by Attorney Dan Saxon; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. I don't know the date. I should be allowed to consult my papers.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: They're right in front of you, tab 3. And if you could stay close to the mike, so each time you don't spend a lot of time trying to get to the mike, it would help us to go a little bit faster. So for your 89(F) statement, signed in B/C/S on the 18th and -- from interviews conducted on the 18th and 19th of September, 2006, you were interviewed by Dan Saxon, Paolo Pastore Stocchi, and another investigator by the name of Marie Costello; right? That is right on the first page of your statement.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And, in addition, there were four interpreters that -- excuse me, three interpreters or four interpreters who participated in the interpretation between you and the investigator and the attorney; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And that statement incorporated items from the first two statements as well as some additional information; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now, if you could go to paragraph 46. So not only did it incorporate the previous statements and add additional information, the interviewers sometimes asked you questions that you didn't know the answer to; right? Mr. Rankic, did they sometimes ask you questions that you didn't know the answer to?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were many such questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And, for example, in paragraphs 46 and 47 -- paragraph 46, I read: "I do not know whether Seselj ever met with Pavlovic/Popovic in person." At the beginning of paragraph 47: "I do not know anything about the relationship between Brano Grujic and Seselj." So the statement also captured the type of information that you gave as well as the information that you didn't know; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were all sorts of information; ones, others, the third type of information.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So if the OTP were crafting a statement to suit its own purpose, it would -- the representatives would have just put in the information they wanted. They wouldn't have put down your response, which was: "I do not know."

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not saying that the OTP changed absolutely everything in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Just the ones that are not favourable to Mr. Seselj --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, Ms. Biersay is quite rightly telling you that if the OTP had wanted to conceal a number of things, these things would not have been mentioned. In paragraph 46, what is mentioned is extremely important for us Judges. It has to do with a meeting of the Serbian Radical Party in Mali Zvornik in mid-April 1992. You say in paragraph 46 that this meeting was held, and you say: "I know that Seselj was there or that he took part in that meeting." However, after that you say that Pavlovic and Seselj may have met, but you cannot confirm that because you were not there. What I'm interested in is this: Was Mr. Seselj at this meeting in Zvornik in April 1992; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe that I said that already yesterday. The rally of the Serbian Chetnik Movement took place in 1990. There was no rally in Mali Zvornik in 1992 of the Serbian Radical Party, because the armed conflicts were ongoing in Bosnia at the time and you can only imagine what would have happened if any such rally had taken place. There would be a lot of dead people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, sir, why, in your own language in paragraph 46, do you say that this meeting took place? This is what I'm trying to understand. And you signed this statement in your own language, and this is what Ms. Biersay is highlighting.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The OTP suggested that they had witnesses who can prove that there was a rally in 1992, that they have statements to that effect by other witnesses, although I claimed that it was in 1990. And finally I said, Well, maybe, maybe there was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a question. Notwithstanding the rally and an important meeting, was there just a simple visit by Mr. Seselj in Mali Zvornik in April 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really don't remember any such thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have another short question for you. You said to the Prosecutor that you wanted to denounce misconduct of the OTP when you came to testify before the Trial Chamber. Could you explain to us, please, why two subpoenas needed to be issued for you to come and testify? We had great difficulty in serving the document on you. We had to resort to the Ministry of the Interior to do so. Could you enlighten us on this, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course. First of all, I work in construction, which means that I am rarely in Belgrade. I work all over the place. That's the first reason. The second reason were my health problems. I have medical documentation that I forwarded to the Trial Chamber to explain why I couldn't come when I was subpoenaed. In other words, every time I couldn't come, I could justify those absences by valid medical documentation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Biersay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: After you signed the B/C/S version or the original of your statement from September 2006, you again had a meeting with VWS to confirm the relocation plans; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: The Registrar, not the OTP, approved your relocation to The Hague, and the plan was for you to come one month before you were to testify and stay for one month after your testimony in The Hague; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't remember those details.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: You, with the assistance of members of VWS, did, in fact, relocate to The Hague on October 6, 2006; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately. I don't know how to explain. I was told that I was under threat in Belgrade, and that's why -- one of the reasons for which I had to go to The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: But in June 2006, you reported to the OTP about threats being made against you and your family; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're talking about the case involving my son that I mentioned just a while ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Mr. Rankic, let's not --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It has nothing to do with what happened later.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Let's not make this longer than it needs to be. You reported threats in June of 2006, and in July of 2006 VWS had already started taking action in order to address your threat issues; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They started to deal with it, but that was not the only reason. There was another reason. I was told that all my statements had been stolen at the Belgrade Airport and that I needed to come to The Hague to re-give all my statements.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And you were told about your statements being taken -- you were told about that in September of 2006, well after you reported the threats in June of 2006; right? You have to say, Yes, into the microphone. That's why I suggested that you sit closer. You're nodding your head.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Biersay, do not forget that the witness has a back problem, which might explain why he leans back.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Could we get a portable microphone, then? Maybe it would simplify things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just proceed for the time the way things are.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So let me rephrase the question or ask the question again.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: The issue of you relocating to Sweden came up in June of 2006, when you suggested the country to the OTP and later to VWS; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At that time, I was in a hopeless situation in Serbia, without a job. I had just divorced.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'm sure we'll -- Mr. Seselj will get into all of those with you. What I would like to know is: You were relocated to --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. Ms. Biersay cannot suggest what I'm going to deal with. Maybe I'll deal with Ms. Biersay, herself, in my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, let Ms. Biersay continue. She quite rightly believes that you are going to address this part of the questions. I also believe that you will address this line of questions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All the better, we shall gain some time.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Let's fast-forward. You arrived in The Hague, is that right, in October of 2006?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And VWS took care of getting you a place to stay, an apartment; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: You had a stipend of 25 Euros a day; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: They gave you a special ID to allow you to move freely in the Netherlands; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Netherlands, probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: You had your own key to the apartment? You could come and go in the apartment whenever you wanted to; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And you stayed in The Hague from October 2006, and you left in December of 2006; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And while you were here, you met two more times -- well, more than two more times, but you signed two more statements, one an addendum to the September 2006 statement. So you signed an addendum in October of 2006; correct? And that is at tab 4 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And that, too, was in your language; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same system, an electronic version on the laptop. It was later printed, and I signed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And you signed the version in your language; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, without reading it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: The first addendum to the statement made corrections to the September 2006 statement, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were certain corrections that needed to be made.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And in December of 2006, you decided to leave. And on December 4th, 2006, you called VWS to let them know that you had left; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. I called them only when I got back to Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what you told them was that you left because your son had fallen ill; specifically, he had a ruptured appendix. That's what you told VWS; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did say that, but that was not the truth.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And you called them the next day, on December 5th, 2006. You again called them to give them an update on your son's condition. That's what you told them in December of 2006, on the 5th of December, 2006; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just said I had made up the reason to leave The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'm not interested in your reason right now. I am interested in what you did. And what you did on the 5th of December, 2006, was to give them a second call to let them know how things were with your son; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right, so that they don't issue a bulletin, an all-points bulletin for me.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And you spoke to them again in January of 2007, and you confirmed that you didn't want to go -- to be relocated to Sweden anymore and that you were going to stay in Serbia; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, because in the meantime they had not done anything, and I had checked that through the Swedish Embassy.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Do you know a man by the name of Ljubisa Petkovic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: When was your last contact with him?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are neighbours in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Do you know a man by the name of Zoran Drazilovic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course, but I don't remember when I saw him last.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So back to my question about Ljubisa Petkovic. He's your neighbour. Did you see him before coming here to The Hague?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not just before I came to The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Did you see Ljubisa Petkovic after you returned to Serbia in January of 2007?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see Ljubisa Petkovic very often, and I probably saw him when I returned.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And you see him so often that when you were issued to appear by summons in November 2007 to talk to OTP representatives, you gave him a document to give to the Prosecution on your behalf, the doctor -- the medical records?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true. I gave those papers to my lawyer, Zoran Stojkovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And do you know someone by the name of Petar Jojic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He's an MP from the Serbian Radical Party.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Do you know that there's documentation listing him as the person delivering the objections that we just talked about at the very beginning of your testimony today, that it was Petar Jojic who delivered the objections you said your lawyer drafted? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Delivered to whom, Ms. Biersay?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Delivered to the field office in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really don't know to whom

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: him implicitly.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And it's after you left The Hague and went back to Serbia that you started signing Defence statements claiming misconduct on the part of people working for the Tribunal; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only individuals among them, not all the people working for the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And if we could go back to that first document that we looked at, and if we could go to page 2. And that would be the 24 December 2007 objections to the subpoena.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And I will read for you: "I have given a number of statements stating that I am threatened by the Office of the Prosecutor, which had kidnapped me and held me for several months in confinement in the Netherlands." That's the document that you signed that was prepared by your lawyer; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: In the third full paragraph on that page, and it should be -- this document is tab 6 in your binder 1, Your Honours: "This should be enough to understand that the Office of the Prosecutor has misled Trial Chamber III, and if this subpoena should remain valid, then Trial Chamber III is not protecting me, but rather throwing me into the embrace and delivering me to those who had kidnapped me and mistreated me." That's what you wrote in your objections from December 2007; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I signed the subpoena drafted by my legal counsel. I mean the objections to the subpoena.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: You testified, when we first started, that you agreed with everything that was in this document. And, in fact, it repeats what you have said in other Defence statements about being kidnapped by the Office of the Prosecutor; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's not a traditional kidnapping, but I was lured here by deceit.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So you're telling --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I noted, in a document that the Judges have, that you said that you had been kidnapped, thanks to the questions that were put to you by Ms. Biersay, that you had the key to your apartment, and that therefore you could move freely. Had you been kidnapped, why stay here? But, in fact, you remained several months in the Netherlands, and you could move freely in this country. This is not how someone who has been kidnapped would find themselves.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, apart from a little paper bearing a number, I had no personal documents. All my documents were in the hands of the OTP, including my passports -- passport during that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So when you were staying in this apartment, you had no passport?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. And if I understand correctly, you received your passport in December.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Was this passport given to you before you returned to Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Your Honours, as the Court is aware, there was a correction to a notice that was given by VWS, and now I will turn to the witness and ask you the following question:

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Isn't it true that you had your passport when you landed in the Netherlands; you had your passport? It was given to you, it was returned to you, right, by VWS?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not right. After passing through Immigration at the Belgrade Airport, and until the beginning of December, my passport was with the VWS.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: First you said the passport was with OTP. Now you're saying it's with VWS. Isn't it true that VWS only had your passport from October 9th of 2006 until 7 November 2006, because your visa needed to be extended and they needed to submit it for that purpose? Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know what the division of work is between different services here, but the fact is that I didn't have the passport in my hands until early December.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Isn't it true that you were given your passport with the extended visa on November 7th, 2006?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not on the 7th of November, but early December.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: You left on December 4th [realtime transcript read in error "in November"] of 2006, so what is it that you mean by "early December"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe there is a mistake. You said that you left on the 4th of December, and it says "in November 2006." So I believe there is a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So if representatives of VWS say that they gave you the passport with the extended visa in November of 2006, you're saying that that's not true; is that what you're telling this Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. If I remember well, I got my passport back on the 1st of December, 1996 [as interpreted], together with money for the next month, which was December, I mean the allowance.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: The translation said "1996." Did you mean 1996, or did you mean 2006?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, I meant 2006.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So just so I understand what you're telling the Trial Chamber, you're saying that everyone that handled your relocation with VWS, that everyone that participated in your interviews, all 17 interpreters and investigators and at least one attorney, that all those people conspired to threaten and kidnap you to give evidence against the accused, in the form of these statements? That's what you're telling the Trial Chamber here today?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, by no means. I can only -- I can only really say that two persons have not been fair and decent towards me.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I ask how much time I have?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think that you have very much left, but the Registrar will tell us.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: While we're checking, Your Honour, I am prepared to -- whatever bit I have left, I'd like to reserve. And I'd also like to indicate that we seek to tender all the 2003 [sic] statements. So for the record -- three. So it would be 65 ter numbers 7540, 7541 -- I'm sorry, it should say "2006 statements." In the transcript, it says "2003." So 7540, 7541, and 7542, and we'd submit that it falls under 89(C) as well as 92 quinquies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You will have 38 minutes left. So we shall have our break, and then after that Mr. Seselj will start putting his questions to the witness, and we'll move on from then. So we'll have a 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The court is back in session. Mr. Seselj will have two hours, and it's up to him to divide those two hours between the main questions and the additional questions. So Ms. Biersay wants to ask additional questions on redirect, but Mr. Seselj will take the floor last, as it was promised.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Rankic, let me just show you one piece of evidence which confirms your claims that The Hague investigators ill-treated you in a horrible way. This was provided to me by the OTP. The document is signed by Mr. Mathias Marcussen. He did not disclose the original of the document. He just told me or relayed the statement of a woman called Marina Krstic who was an interpreter during the first interview.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Marcussen informed me that Ms. Marina Krstic has stated that on the 5th, which was on the second day of your interview, you voiced very serious objections with regard to the chronology of the statement, and that you stated as follows: "You told me during the two days to stick to the chronology, and now look what you've done. This doesn't make any sense. Everything is hickledy-pickledy. This statement is shit. If the whole Tribunal works in the same manner, I will never go there to testify."

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. Could we clarify which statement he's referring to? I believe it's the very first one from 2003.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first statement from 2003, the statement provided on the 4th and 5th of August, the only one provided on those dates. And I am reading from a letter by Mr. Marcussen sent to me, in which he says: "Dear Mr. Seselj," and I would like to thank Mr. Marcussen. Do you have that letters, Your Honours? Maybe I could give you a copy if you don't have one. Do you have it or not? You do; good. Okay, fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So once you said that that statement was shit, Marina Krstic, according to Mr. Marcussen's interpretation, stated as follows: "Mr. Rankic's words were, indeed, interpreted. It was very tense. When Mr. Paolo Pastore Stocchi tore up certain pages and he turned towards the monitor and started changing paragraphs, and he also put subtitles above some of them and changed the order of the paragraphs." And then Mr. Rankic repeated some of the objections. I interpreted them. Mr. Paolo Stocchi put his finger in the left ear, very theatrically, and said, I can't concentrate if you both speak at the same time. Mr. Rankic smiled ironically and said: "I'm going to sign your statement because I trust this woman." He pointed at Ms. Krstic. And then: "Let's all go home." And later on, according to Mr. Marcussen's interpretation, Ms. Krstic said as follows: "Later on, Mr. Rankic signed the statement, and that statement had never been properly translated for him." In other words, Ms. Marina Krstic confirms that you are telling the truth, Mr. Rankic, and not Ms. Biersay. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I don't know what else is there in Ms. Krstic's statement. I wish I'd received it in its totality. Mr. Marcussen was kind enough, and ex officio he was also obliged to provide me with at least some of the parts. So Ms. Biersay actually ill-treated you for an hour and a half to no avail, because here's the proof that you didn't fair too well during that conversation.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an understatement. It was even worse than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It is my impression that you were telling the truth in the statements provided to my associates, and that under duress you accepted to sign some things, fully well aware of the fact that they were not truthful. And before we embark on those things, and that is very important for me -- fortunately enough, we are in open session, and what is important for me is for the Serbian public to realise how untruthful things are that are mentioned here. This just one thing that I would like to ask you. You were promised that you would be provided with a good apartment, a good job, and a good salary in Sweden, and that you would be able to remain in Sweden, living there forever; is that true?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, something to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then towards the end, or in the course of December 2006, they told you this: You are going to Sweden, but only for three months; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Allegedly, the Swedish government had to be in agreement. That's how I understood it. An application was filed with the Swedish government, and the answer was pending.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You could go to Sweden, but only for three months, which means you would not have been given an apartment, a job, a salary?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose that was the end result.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You felt deceived, and that's why you decided to leave Holland and go to Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And because you were disappointed in The Hague Tribunal, you turned to my associates and you decided to be a Defence witness; is that true?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And now I'm going to speculate a little. Please do not be offended if -- I am not trying to embarrass you. If you had been given the ownership of a good apartment in Sweden, if you had been given a good job, a good salary in Sweden, if you had been provided with Swedish citizenship, would you, in that case, confirm here in the courtroom that all those false allegations from your five statements are actually correct and truthful? Would you do it for the love of the apartment, the job, and the salary?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everybody who knows, and a lot of Serbian people know what kind of a man I am, would know that I would never do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now I'm going to disappoint both the Trial Chamber and the OTP, and I will not follow up on any of Ms. Biersay's questions. I'm interested in the financial aspect of the problem. Let's start with first things first. Let's follow the paragraphs in the first, second, and third statement. In your first statement in 2003, in paragraph 9 you stated, and the OTP recorded it on your behalf, that: "Vuk Draskovic and Seselj founded the Serbian Freedom Movement, which couldn't last long." Could you have told them something like that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because I'm aware of the chronology of the events.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The entire Serbian general public knows that with a group of intellectuals, I founded the Serbian Freedom Movement when we signed the foundation document on the 6th of January, 1990, and that Vuk Draskovic was not involved in that. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So it is an absolute lie, and the entire Serbian general public knows that it is a lie. And then it goes on to say: "They split, and each of them founded their own parties. Seselj founded the Serbian Chetnik Pokret, and Vuk Draskovic founded the Serbian Renewal Movement." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. First you founded the Serbian Rule Movement together, and then you split, and it was only then that you founded the Serbian Chetnik Movement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Let me add something to that. On the same day when I founded my Serbian Freedom Movement, Vuk Draskovic founded the Serbian National Renewal in Nova Pazova. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mirkovic was the president, and Vuk Draskovic was the vice-president. And then in the beginning of March 1990, Vuk Draskovic was abolished from that movement?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then one wing of the Serbian Renewal joined him?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then we joined the Serbian Freedom Movement with that wing of Draskovic's, and together we founded the Serbian Renewal Movement.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then we excluded Draskovic in the beginning of June 1990 from the Serbian Renewal Movement by a majority vote; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but he didn't want to cede the stamp, if I remember correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then he set up, in the Rolex Restaurant, a new party and called it by the same name; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: For a month, there were two parties called Serbian Renewal Movement.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then we changed our name into Serbian Chetnik Movement primarily in order to stop having problems with Draskovic. Is paragraph 9 in the statement completely untruthful?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It is very important for me that the entire Serbian general public will see that. Further on in paragraph 13, it says that you were one of the founders of the Serbian Chetnik Movement, as a matter of a fact one of the 100 signatories of the founding document that had to be submitted for registration.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It says here that besides yourself, there were some other people, including Jovan Glamocanin; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know when Jovan Glamocanin joined us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But in any case, he never joined the Serbian Chetnik Movement?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He only joined when the Serbian Radical Party was founded.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These names do not make too much sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So this is also a lie --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Please slow down. The interpreters are unable to follow at this pace. And, Mr. Witness, do observe a small pause between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Let's go on through paragraph 13, and they ascribe this to you: "I believe that this was in December. The regime arrested Vojislav Seselj, and since it was at the time of the first multi-party elections in Serbia, by this the regime removed Seselj from the political scene. In February 1991, Seselj was released from prison." Isn't this an absolute lie, a blatant lie?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know the chronology very well. You were arrested before the presidential elections, but you were released in December to start your campaign.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I was released at the beginning of November, because every evening the state television published news about presidential candidates, and my name was first on the list, "Dr. Vojislav Seselj," a Dr. Lu [phoen], who was the presidential candidate, but sitting in prison; wasn't that the case?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then they released me against my will?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I did not want to sign any documents, I didn't want to leave the prison, and I was forcibly thrown out of the prison.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In my campaign, I held 10 different promotions in Novi Sad, Cacak, Subotica, Kragujevac, Nis, and some other places; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: At the beginning of December, did I not appear on state television? I was given only one hour for my promotion, and I won the entire electoral body?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One part of the electoral body.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Isn't that the time when my popularity took off in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So is all this a blatant lie?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So that was paragraph 13. Let's go on, disguising all the untruths in the statement. In paragraph 14, you're talking about the time when Radical Party was united with the Chetnik Movement, and you say that the Serbian Chetnik Movement was preserved, but more or less the traditional military wing of the future party. In February 1991, was the Serbian Chetnik Movement a military wing of the Serbian Radical Party?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It continued the traditions of Chetnik movement in Serbia which dated back to the turn of the century, and we continued the traditions of the Serbian movement at Ravna Gora, which was an anti-fascist movement during the Second World War.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Was our main objecting [as interpreted] to rehabilitate the Serbian Chetniks that the Communists for decades had accused that it was a whistling movement?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Without any military elements contained therein.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. There were no military actions at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Nobody even knew that there would be a war.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The political situation was tense, but nobody expected that there would be war. Is it correct that you stated, as it was recorded in paragraph 16, that Vojin Vuletic died under suspicious circumstances?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was suggested to me by the investigator. He told me that many of your associates died under very suspicious circumstances. As far as I know, Mr. Vuletic suffered from angina pectoris, if I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And he died of a heart infarction?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I know, but I'm not a medical expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you remember that he as a member of the democratic party? You don't remember that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Who else of my associates died under suspicious circumstances?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have to ask the investigators. They said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So they wanted to qualify me as a killer who killed his disobedient associates. In paragraph 20, it says that the decision to set up the War Staff was made by Seselj, who simply decided that Ljubisa Petkovic had to be the head of the War Staff. Do you know that there was -- that it was decided that Ljubisa Petkovic, as one of the vice-presidents of the party, would be the head of that staff?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a crisis staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes, but it says "War Staff" here; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But is this a blatant lie in paragraph 20.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Does the entire Serbian general public know that this is a blatant lie, whoever knows the history of the Serbian political parties from the 1990s onwards?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a notorious fact in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well. In paragraph 21, it says Minister Cvijan, it says here that personally saw him and that you visited him twice, and that you met with him in order to co-ordinate the deployment of volunteers, and that the minister had more information about the needs for manpower in the field. Isn't that a fabrication?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my introductory speech yesterday, I said that I did go to the ministry with -- for relations with Serbs outside of Serbia with Ljubisa Petkovic, but Ljubisa Petkovic went there on his private matters and I was sitting outside of their office. I was having coffee while he was talking to him about his private problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You don't have to repeat what you said. My time is limited, and the Trial Chamber is always inclined to rob me even of those rights that I am entitled to. Let's not waste time. The Ministry for Serbs Outside of Serbia, could they -- could it be involved in any military matters?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, I can't accept that sentence without saying something. When you say that, The Trial Chamber is always inclined to rob me of those rights that I'm entitled to, this is not based on anything. I know that what you are interested in is the media and the Serbian listeners, but I would like to say that I disagree totally with you in this regard.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's all good and well that you don't agree, but this is the main part of my defence, and this is what I intend to prove in my closing argument.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In paragraph 22, it says: "After Ljubisa Petkovic received requests from local TOs with regard to the deployment of volunteers, he would turn either to the Ministry for Relations with Serbs Outside Serbia or the Ministry of Defence in Serbia because they have better information about the situation in specific areas." Is it entirely impossible for the Ministry for Relations with Serbs Outside of Serbia to deal with military issues?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't deal with military issues. They only assisted us with refugees. They provided us with buses and other such matters that were needed for the deployment of the volunteers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And food for refugees?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, food, accommodation, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And when was it that the Ministry for Relations with Serbs Outside of Serbia provided you with buses? Where did those buses come from?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that those buses belonged to the Territorial Defence, and the Territorial Defence was duty-bound to provide them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: As far as I know, there were sponsors, different companies.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: There were transport companies which provided buses as sponsorship to the Association of Serbs?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't have their own buses, so they could only rely on sponsors.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did the Ministry for Defence of Serbia have any resources that they could use to help us with the deployment of volunteers or with any other military matters?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: This was a formality. Serbia had that ministry, a minister and his secretary, and that was all?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The JNA was still within the competence of the federal state; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So this is another blatant lie, what it says here in paragraph 22. I've never heard before that our volunteers were sent to Lipovaca for additional training, as it says here in paragraph 34. As far as I know, Lipovaca was only the collection area where our volunteers came, as well as volunteers of other parties, as well as individuals who volunteered. And from there they were deployed into JNA units and units of the Territorial Defence. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never mentioned Lipovac. I only mentioned Prigrevica.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: First in Prigrevica before the JNA was engaged in the war, and then Bubanj Potok?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything went through the JNA after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So there was no training in Lipovaca; it was only the collection spot?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment. The interpreters are asking you to slow down. You're going too fast.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, I'll try.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So paragraph 24 is absolutely untruthful, too, and anyone who knows anything will know that. In paragraph 25, it reads that you, the Crisis Staff, knew where our volunteers were, and that you monitored what was going on the ground. But I'm astonished to read the Chetnik commanders came for weekly meetings of the Crisis Staff to make their reports. Is that at all possible? The commander who's in the field would come back every week to make a report.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I said is this: Individual Chetnik commanding officers and commanders, if they happened to be in Belgrade, could come to attend Crisis Staff meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But that's not what it says here. It says they came for weekly meetings, which means they came regularly?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Loads of things are written there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you remember members of the Crisis Staff -- did any of you members of the Crisis Staff know about it, 10 of you? Were any of you experts in military matters?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Only Drazilovic, who had crashed his plane and was a retired pilot of the air force.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And none of you even had the rank of reserve officer?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So you did not know tactical problems, operative problems, let alone strategy. You were only able to assemble volunteers, organise them, and send them where they needed to be sent. Was that your only task?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And to provide them with some food, some cigarettes, arrange with the JNA that they be given uniforms, weapons, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well. So you did not have and were not able to have any command function?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That goes without saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So paragraph 25 is also an outright lie. Paragraph 27 says that my publicity was my greatest priority, followed by quantity and quality?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not exactly true.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Didn't I always insist on quality, then -- and publicity was my third priority?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I meant publicity for the party.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And it says that: "Seselj never told us in the Crisis Staff to familiarise volunteers with the provisions of the Geneva Conventions. In fact, he never even mentioned it." Is this true?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already denied it yesterday and explained that several times -- you, several times Ljubisa Petkovic, and sometimes I, myself, gave them a lecture on how they should conduct themselves on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Are you aware that there are more journalists in Belgrade who remember the sending off of volunteers, where I spoke --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj has put a number of questions to you, Witness, and you are saying the opposite of what you have said so far. Admittedly, one could believe that the volunteers commander came to the War Staff every week and that this would be rather complicated. In the 89(F) statement which you have signed in your own language, we find the following sentence. You say --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, he signed this only in English, not in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, the 89(F) statement was signed in the B/C/S version. Please look at page 11, paragraph 32. You say as follows: "I received reports from units of volunteers over the phone. Sometimes I passed the information on directly to Mr. Seselj. In other instances, I provided the information to Petkovic." So you signed this in your own language. The fact that the commanders of volunteer units sent you reports, what do you have to say to this today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
